chunk_findings.detail:
`_kind` returns `"delta"` whenever `commit` is set or `base` is any value other than `cfg.worktree.base_ref or W.default_branch(repo)`:
```
return "delta" if delta or commit or (base and base != default_base) else "full"
```
In `_scope`, the budget is checked only `if kind == "full" and item`, and the caller records `review_kind = kind` for non-full rounds, which `_full_rounds` explicitly ignores (`... .get("review_kind") == "full"`). So a review invoked with an explicit base — e.g. `ddflow review ITEM --gate G --base HEAD~1000` (or `--commit <sha>`) — reviews the full range from that base to the item's head but is tagged `delta`, is never counted by `_full_rounds`, and is never refused. An agent can therefore run an unbounded number of full-scope, uncounted rounds against a gate simply by always passing `--base <old-commit>`, which defeats the operator's "a per-item `--force --reason` is the recorded exception" requirement (the bypass is neither refused nor recorded as `budget_forced`). This is not the "delta" the intent describes (a recheck since the recorded `reviewed_head`); it is a full re-review of a possibly larger range.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py: `_kind` / `_scope`

chunk_findings.detail: The message is parameterized on `cap` (`[review].max_rounds = {cap}`) but hardcodes the rationale to a cap of two: `"Each round after the second finds fewer defects than the one before"`. Since `max_rounds` is user-configurable (`0 = unlimited`, any N), this is factually inconsistent whenever `cap != 2`. Concrete input: with `review.max_rounds = 5`, after five full rounds the refusal prints `has had 5 full review rounds ([review].max_rounds = 5)` followed by `Each round after the second ...`, i.e. it argues against a third round while having just refused the sixth — wrong guidance in the exact message the operator required to name the alternatives.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py: `_budget_refusal`

chunk_findings.detail: The report path is chosen with `edit.set.strip() not in _BUDGET_KNOBS and "[review]" not in edit.append_toml.replace(" ", "")`. This is a literal-substring test on the appended TOML, so it only fires for the canonical unquoted `[review]` header. Confirmed input: an MCP caller runs `ddflow_configure(append_toml='["review"]\nmax_rounds = 0')`. Quoted table headers are valid TOML and are parsed as the `review` table, but after `.replace(" ", "")` the string is `["review"]\nmax_rounds=0`, which does not contain the substring `[review]` (the `"` intervenes); `edit.set` is empty, so it is not in `_BUDGET_KNOBS` either. The guard returns `out` early: no `session_note` is written and no operator NOTE is appended, yet the budget has been disabled. That silently defeats the stated requirement that "changing the knob over MCP is reported to the operator" (and lets an agent remove the cap without the recorded `--force --reason` exception). Single-quoted `['review']` or a commented `# [review]` line behave the same way (the latter is a false positive rather than a miss), so the guard should key off the parsed section/key rather than a raw-substring match.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py:report_budget_change (the `_BUDGET_KNOBS` / `"[review]"` guard)

chunk_findings.detail:
The shipped driver template tells every project's agent that the cap is changed with `ddflow config --set review.max_rounds N [--local]`, and `ddflow/templates/prompts/help/gates.md` repeats the same `ddflow config --set review.max_rounds N` form. The change's own specification of the CLI is positional: "the CLI (`ddflow config review.max_rounds 0 [--local]`)" — key and value, no `--set` flag (the only config flags named are `--local` and `--explain`). Since these files are the shipped templates that `ddflow init`/`ddflow prompts` hand to agents in every project, the documented remediation path is the one that gets executed verbatim: an operator (or agent) follows the driver text and runs `ddflow config --set review.max_rounds 0`; with the specified grammar the `--set` token is an unrecognized option (or, worse, is swallowed as the key), so the cap is not changed and the user is stuck at the default with a refusal that points them at a command that does not work. Either the templates must use the positional form (`ddflow config review.max_rounds N [--local]`), or the implementation has to actually accept `--set`; as written, docs and spec cannot both be true.

Note: the rest of the part (default 2, third full round refused with exit 3, delta/triage always allowed, `--force --reason` recorded, `max_rounds = 0` unlimited, `on_exceed = "warn"`, MCP reporting of `review.*` changes) matches the stated acceptance criteria, and the `docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md` copy is byte-identical to the shipped template, which the generality rule permits.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md (new "Review rounds are budgeted" paragraph)

chunk_findings.detail: This test asserts the shipped default by calling `Config.load()` with no project argument, so it reads whatever ambient configuration the machine/environment currently has, instead of a clean throwaway project. The feature being added explicitly introduces an environment override for exactly these knobs (`test_every_layer_changes_it` proves `Config.load(repo, env={"DDFLOW_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS": "5", ...})` yields `max_rounds == 5` and source `env`), which means the env layer is consulted from the real environment. Concrete failure: with `DDFLOW_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=5` exported (a documented, supported way to change the knob), `Config.load()` returns `cfg.review.max_rounds == 5` and `cfg.sources["review.max_rounds"] == "env"`, so the assertions `(2, "refuse")` and `== "default"` both fail even though the shipped default is correct. The same leak affects `test_a_fresh_init_project_has_the_budget_with_no_config_line` (line 232) unless the `repo` fixture scrubs the environment. The test should use the `repo` fixture / an explicit empty `env` (as the "fresh project" test already does for its config-file claim) so that the default is asserted hermetically rather than against the operator's live machine configuration.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_budget.py:74 (`test_the_default_is_two_rounds_then_refuse_for_every_project`)

chunk_findings.detail: The round-budget documentation defines a full round as "a review of the item's whole diff", but then declares a `--base <ref>` review (and a `--commit` review) to be "not [a full round] … and … never refused". Scope is a property of the ref, not of the flag: for item T1 whose diff is `B..HEAD`, `ddflow review T1 --gate critic --base B` reviews the whole item diff, i.e. exactly a full round by the README's own definition, yet it is uncounted. So given T1 already at 2 recorded full rounds, `ddflow review T1 --gate critic --base B` returns success and runs another whole-diff review instead of the refusal (exit 3) that the acceptance criterion requires ("the third full round on a gate is refused"); repeating it runs unlimited full rounds. Because the criterion's purpose is to bound full rounds per item (operator: "A cap of 2 full review rounds, then triage"), counting by invocation flag rather than by covered range leaves the cap defeatable by an agent that reaches for `--base` (or `--commit` on a single-commit item) instead of `--delta`. Either such reviews must be counted as full rounds when their range is the item's whole diff, or the README must not advertise them as an uncounted, never-refused path.
chunk_findings.title: README.md (review-round budget paragraph, ~line 1160)

chunk_findings.detail: `_full_rounds` deliberately counts from the event log so that "a later delta, a manual `gate skip`/`record` or a re-claim replaces that record's evidence" cannot reset the budget (see its own docstring). `_delta_scope`, however, takes the head that `--delta` diffs from out of `it.gates.get(gate).evidence["reviewed_head"]` — i.e. out of exactly the record that the re-claim/`gate skip`/`gate record` path replaces. Concrete scenario: item X records two full rounds at gate G (cap = 2, `on_exceed = refuse`), so `_full_rounds` returns 2 and any further full round is refused; the user then re-claims the item (or runs `ddflow gate record G ...`). The evidence is replaced, `reviewed_head` is gone, so `_delta_scope` returns `"--delta rechecks what changed since the head of the item's recorded G review, and none is on record: run the full review first."` The delta is thereby blocked, and the escape it suggests — a full round — is blocked by `_budget` because the count survived the re-claim. The item is deadlocked, violating "a delta review and a triage are never refused" and the stated goal that after the cap the delta recheck of the fix commits stays ALWAYS allowed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_delta_scope (reading `reviewed_head` from the gate record)

chunk_findings.detail: `_kind` returns `"delta"` whenever `base and base != default_base`. In `_scope`, `kind == "full"` is the only path that calls `_budget`, and `_round_evidence`/`_full_rounds` only count rounds tagged `"full"`. So a request that reviews the item's whole diff against an explicit base that differs from `cfg.worktree.base_ref`/default branch — e.g. `ddflow review X --gate G --base origin/main` where `base_ref` is `main` — is tagged `"delta"`, is never budget-checked and is never counted. An agent can therefore run unlimited full-scope reviews past the cap by adding a `--base` argument, and a custom workflow whose review invocation always passes an integration base will silently never trigger `max_rounds` at all, defeating D-review-budget's "agents may NOT raise or disable it for an item without the operator".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_kind (non-default `--base` classified as delta)

chunk_findings.detail: The new docstring defines a FULL round as one with "no `chunks`, `delta`, `commit` or a `base` other than the default", i.e. an explicit `--commit` or a non-default `--base` makes the run *not* a full round, so it is neither counted nor capped. But `ddflow review <id> --gate G --base <merge-base of branch>` produces exactly the same review content as the default (uncounted) full round: same diff, same reviewers, same findings. So with `[review].max_rounds = 2`, after two recorded full rounds an agent (or any caller) can keep generating unlimited full reviews by appending `--base <non-default>` (or `--commit HEAD`), with no `--force`, no `--reason`, no record, and no refusal. That directly defeats "bound full review rounds per gate per item" and the operator's hard requirement that "agents may NOT raise or disable it for an item without the operator", since the recorded round count would stay at 2 while arbitrarily many full-diff reviews are actually performed. The refusal's advertised alternatives (`--delta`, `triage`, `--force --reason`) are therefore not the only paths past the cap. The chunk re-run path (`--chunks ...`, which re-reviews a chunk of the full diff and is likewise classified as non-full) is a further un-counted way to re-run reviewers past the cap.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/review.py `_scope` full-round classification (per the new docstring of `review()`)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py `_scope` full-round classification (per the new docstring of `review()`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new refusal `Outcome` builds `data={"id": item, "gate": gate, "outcome": "", "findings": [], "text": why}` and drops the `"how"` key that the equivalent refusal it replaces carried (`data={..., "how": how, ...}`, from the old `_rerun_scope` error branch). Every other review outcome in this file, including the failure/`unavailable` helpers, includes `how` to describe the diff source. Concretely, a refused chunk re-run such as `ddflow review 42 --gate impl --chunks 99` (invalid chunk spec) now returns an outcome whose `data` has no `"how"`, whereas before this change the same path returned `data["how"]`; any consumer that reads `data["how"]` from a review outcome (which the API previously guaranteed for refusals as well) now hits `KeyError`/missing-field.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/review.py refusal outcome in `review()` (`if why:` branch)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py refusal outcome in `review()` (`if why:` branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The note's revert instruction is hard-coded to `review.max_rounds`, regardless of which knob was actually changed. Given the MCP call `ddflow_configure` setting `review.on_exceed = "warn"` (a budget knob in `_BUDGET_KNOBS`, so the function does not early-return), `what` is correctly built as `"review.on_exceed = warn"`, but the note then tells the operator: *"if you did not ask for this change, revert it with `ddflow config --set review.max_rounds 2`"*. That command changes `max_rounds` only and leaves `on_exceed = warn` in place, so an operator who follows the advice exactly still has a weakened budget: the next third full round warns instead of being refused (exit 3), which is precisely the behaviour the cap is supposed to guarantee. The same mismatch occurs for the appended-table branch (`what = "the [review] table (appended TOML)"`), where reverting `max_rounds` alone does not revert the appended `on_exceed`/`max_rounds` pair. The revert hint should be derived from `what` (or name the actual key/value that was changed, e.g. `review.on_exceed refuse` for this case) rather than unconditionally pointing at `ReviewConfig().max_rounds`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py::report_budget_change

chunk_findings.detail: The change instructs users to change the cap with `ddflow config --set review.max_rounds N [--local]` (implement-phase.md) and `ddflow config --set review.max_rounds N` (gates.md, plus the mirrored copy in docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md). The interface this feature actually exposes — as stated in the task's own layer enumeration, "the CLI (`ddflow config review.max_rounds 0 [--local]`)" — takes the key and value as positional arguments (`ddflow config review.max_rounds 0 --local`), with no `--set` flag. A user (or an agent reading the driver/help prompt) who follows the shipped documentation and runs `ddflow config --set review.max_rounds 0` will hit an unrecognized-flag/usage error, so the documented "how to change it" path does not work; only the README/`config --explain` knob documentation requirement is undermined, and the "The refusal message names how to change it" acceptance is not actually satisfiable by the command the docs advertise. Either the docs must use the positional form or the CLI must add `--set`; they currently disagree.

chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/implement-phase.md (added "Review rounds are budgeted" paragraph) and ddflow/templates/prompts/help/gates.md (added paragraph)

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts the shipped default with `Config.load()` (no repository argument), so it does not read a fresh/throwaway project — it resolves whatever configuration is ambient for the process (the current working directory's `[review]` table, the machine-local `.ddflow/local/config.toml`, and the process environment). Every other test in this file explicitly passes the `repo` fixture, and `Config.load(repo, env={...})` elsewhere proves the loader consults `os.environ` by default. So a developer or CI machine that has exercised the very layers this feature advertises — e.g. `DDFLOW_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=5` exported, or a prior `ddflow config --set review.max_rounds 0 --local` run in the ddflow checkout — makes `cfg.review.max_rounds` come back as `5`/`0` and `cfg.sources["review.max_rounds"]` as `"env"`/`"local"`, and the assertions `(2, "refuse")` / `sources == "default"` fail even though the dataclass default in `ddflow/config.py` is correct. The generality acceptance explicitly requires "tests build a fresh throwaway project" and prove the default there; using the ambient `Config.load()` (the dataclass default is what is being checked, so `Config()` or `Config.load(tmp_repo)` is the right call) both violates that and makes the test non-hermetic. If `Config.load`'s `repo` parameter is not optional, the same line instead raises `TypeError` at collection time.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_budget.py:60 `test_the_default_is_two_rounds_then_refuse_for_every_project`

chunk_findings.detail: The revised definition says a `--commit <sha>` or `--base <ref>` review "at or after the head the gate's last review covered" is not a full round because it "can only be narrower." That is true for `--base` (a base at/after `reviewed_head` makes `base..HEAD` a subset of the previously reviewed `reviewed_head..HEAD`), but it is not true for `--commit`: a commit *strictly after* the head the last review covered is content the gate has never recorded a review over. The stated principle is "a full round is any review that can cover the item's whole diff," yet the rule exempts exactly the case where new, unreviewed commits are introduced. Concretely, with `reviewed_head = C3` and item head `C5`, `ddflow review <id> --gate G --commit C4` and `--commit C5` are both exempt from the budget, so an agent can land fixes as new commits and keep reviewing each one with `--commit` forever without ever spending a full round — the cap never binds and later-round findings are never forced through triage. Either the `--commit` clause should be dropped (only `--base` reaches back past the head), or the "before the head" case is the one that is already covered and therefore the genuinely narrower one; as written the two flags are lumped under a rationale that only holds for `--base`.
chunk_findings.title: README.md:1148-1155 (review-budget paragraph)

chunk_findings.detail: `_kind` uses the last reviewed head as the sole pivot, so any ref that lies between the item's base and that head is misclassified as a full round, even though its diff is a strict subset of what the previous review already covered and therefore cannot "cover the item's whole diff". Concrete input: an item based on `main` whose gate was fully reviewed at head `H`; a later `ddflow review <id> --gate G --commit <C>` (or `--base <C>`) where `C` is an ordinary commit with `base ⪯ C ⪯ H` produces the diff `C..HEAD` / `C`'s own changes — strictly narrower than the reviewed range — but `git merge-base --is-ancestor H C` exits non-zero, so `_kind` returns `"full"`. Once `[review].max_rounds` (default 2) rounds are recorded, that narrow review is refused with exit 3, and the offered escape hatches don't help: `--delta` scopes from `H`, so it cannot express `C..HEAD`, leaving only `--force`. Before this change `_kind` returned `"delta"` for *any* `--commit`/custom `--base`, so this is a regression that blocks a previously allowed narrow review, contradicting the documented definition of a full round.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_kind

chunk_findings.detail: `_budget_keys` short-circuits on `if edit.set:` and, when `set` is non-empty, inspects *only* `edit.set`, entirely ignoring `edit.append_toml`. The previous condition it replaces (`edit.set.strip() not in _BUDGET_KNOBS and "[review]" not in edit.append_toml...`) proceeded whenever *either* the set key was a budget knob *or* the appended TOML touched `[review]`. Concrete bypass: an MCP/CLI call that carries both a non-budget `set` and budget knobs in the append, e.g. `ddflow config --set gate.unit_tests.command 'pytest -q' --append-toml '[review]\nmax_rounds = 0'` (or the equivalent `ddflow_configure` payload). `edit.set` is truthy, `norm("gate.unit_tests.command")` matches nothing in `_BUDGET_KNOBS`, so `_budget_keys` returns `[]`, and `report_budget_change` hits `if not touched: return out` — the review budget was changed over MCP but the operator note ("NOTE FOR THE OPERATOR: the review budget was changed over MCP …") is never emitted. This silently defeats the requirement that a knob change over MCP be reported to the operator, which is the whole point of the recorded exception; the old code reported it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py:310 (`_budget_keys`)

chunk_findings.detail: If `append_toml` sets `review` to a truthy non-table scalar, the list comprehension iterates a non-iterable. Input: `--append-toml 'review = 1'` (or `review = true`). `tomllib.loads(...).get("review")` returns `1`/`True`, which is truthy, so `[f"review.{k}" for k in table if ...]` raises `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable` instead of returning `[]`. The `if table else []` guard only catches empty/falsy values, not wrong-typed ones, so this propagates out of `report_budget_change` (MCP configure / `ddflow config`) as an unhandled exception.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py:312 (`_budget_keys`, `for k in table`)

chunk_findings.detail:
This test asserts that a delta review is refused:

```python
def test_a_refusal_carries_how(repo, tmp_path):
    _setup(repo, tmp_path)
    out = api.review(repo, gate="critic", item="T1", delta=True)
    assert out.exit == REFUSED and "how" in out.data
```

With no prior review on the item, `delta=True` can compute no base. The stated invariant is absolute and is repeated three times: "a delta review and a triage are never refused", "delta and triage still work", and "a delta recheck of the fix commits and `ddflow review triage` stay ALWAYS allowed". Either:

- the implementation treats `delta=True` with no prior full review as an ordinary (allowed) review — in which case this test fails: it gets `OK`, not `REFUSED`, so the test encodes the opposite of the spec; or
- the implementation does refuse a delta with no base — in which case the shipped behaviour violates the documented invariant, and this test is the one that locks the violation in.

Either way the test is wrong against the intent. Also note it never reaches the budget refusal it claims to exercise (only two full rounds trigger that), so `"how" in out.data` is being satisfied by a non-budget refusal path (missing delta base), and the acceptance criterion "the third full round on a gate is refused with the alternatives" is not actually covered here.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_budget.py::test_a_refusal_carries_how

chunk_findings.detail:
`_budget_keys` returns as soon as `edit.set` is truthy, without ever looking at `edit.append_toml`:

```python
if edit.set:
    return [k for k in _BUDGET_KNOBS if norm(edit.set) == k]
```

A `ConfigEdit` carries both `set` and `append_toml` (both are read in this same function, and the previous code deliberately evaluated both with `edit.set... not in _BUDGET_KNOBS **and** "[review]" not in edit.append_toml...`). So an edit that sets one non-budget key and appends a `[review]` table is representable, e.g. `ConfigEdit(set="gate.unit_tests.command", value="pytest -q", append_toml="[review]\nmax_rounds = 0")`. With that input:

- `edit.set` is truthy → the function returns `[]` (no budget knob matched), and `report_budget_change` hits `if not touched: return out`.
- The `[review]` `max_rounds = 0` (or `on_exceed = "warn"`) change therefore goes completely unreported: no operator note, no session note, no revert hint.

The old code did **not** return in this case (`"[review]" in edit.append_toml` made the `and` condition false, so it proceeded to emit the note), so this is a regression, not a pre-existing gap. The same branch also drops the "other" knob when `--set review.max_rounds ...` is combined with an append that changes `review.on_exceed`: `touched` will list only the `--set` knob and the generated revert command omits the appended one.

Concrete demonstrating input: an MCP `ddflow_configure` edit with `set="gate.unit_tests.command"`, `value="pytest -q"`, `append_toml="[review]\nmax_rounds = 0"` → `_budget_keys` returns `[]` → `report_budget_change` returns `out` unchanged, so the operator is never told the review budget was disabled over MCP.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup.py `_budget_keys` / `report_budget_change`

chunk_findings.detail: The new flag-less form is implemented asymmetrically with the `--set` form. With `--set`, every positional word after the key is joined into the value (`return a.set, " ".join(words)`), so a value can be arbitrary whitespace-containing text. With the flag-less form the code only accepts *exactly* two words (`if len(words) == 2: return words[0], words[1]`) and otherwise returns `("", "")`. So `ddflow config review.max_rounds 0` works, but any value that is passed as more than one shell token (e.g. `ddflow config review.on_exceed warn now`, or an accidental extra token such as `ddflow config review.max_rounds 0 extra`) yields `key == ""`. `cmd_config` then calls `A.configure(..., set="", value="")` and, because the confirmation branch is guarded by `if key:`, prints no "key = value" line at all — the command exits without ever writing the requested setting, and the user has no signal that the value was dropped. The equivalent `--set review.on_exceed warn now` path would have written `warn now`, so the two documented spellings disagree for the same intended value, and the flag-less spelling silently no-ops instead of either writing the value or rejecting the input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/setup.py `_config_key_value` (lines ~149-156)
